item.text:
## 2B.10 Research Note: Vladimir Putin, Russia, 2023

**Working judgment:** **No.** Putin left regional/international relations **less peaceful, less stable, and less lawful** in 2023. There were some formal diplomatic signals and multilateral contacts, but the year’s concrete moves were more important: continued war-related coercion, the suspension of New START, tactical nuclear deployment in Belarus, and an ICC arrest warrant.

### Accepted claims

- **Title:** `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 31.03.2023 г. № 229`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 31 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia’s updated foreign-policy concept states support for strategic stability, arms control, nonproliferation, and reducing nuclear and WMD risk, while also emphasizing multilateral diplomacy and conflict prevention. This is the best pro-restraint evidence, but it is declaratory doctrine and did not translate into a safer international environment in 2023.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.4`, `1B.7`

- **Title:** `Совместное заявление Российской Федерации и Китайской Народной Республики об углублении отношений...`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 21 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://special.kremlin.ru/supplement/5920](https://special.kremlin.ru/supplement/5920)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin and Xi issued a joint statement that welcomed dialogue on Ukraine and framed responsible discussion as preferable to uncontrolled escalation. This shows Putin still had some active diplomatic channels, but it was not a concrete peace settlement or a lawful resolution of the war.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.10`, `2B.7`, `2B.1`

- **Title:** `Informal meeting of the CIS heads of state`  
  **Publisher:** President of Russia / Kremlin  
  **Date:** 26 Dec 2023  
  **URL:** [https://en.special.kremlin.ru/catalog/keywords/82/events/73171](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/catalog/keywords/82/events/73171)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin hosted CIS leaders in St. Petersburg and held bilateral meetings with Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. This shows continued regional diplomatic activity and some stability in relations with nearby partners, but it does not offset the broader deterioration in Europe and the Ukraine war.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.10`, `1B.8`

- **Title:** `Putin says Russia's participation in New START is suspended`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Gulf News  
  **Date:** 21 Feb 2023  
  **URL:** [https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764](https://gulfnews.com/world/europe/russias-putin-issues-new-nuclear-warnings-to-west-over-ukraine-1.1676971364764)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin suspended Russia’s participation in New START and threatened renewed nuclear testing. That made international security less lawful and less stable, and it undercut existing arms-control architecture rather than preserving it.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.10`, `1B.4`, `1B.7`, `1B.8`

- **Title:** `Russia signs deal to deploy tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 25 May 2023  
  **URL:** [https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/](https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia formalized deployment of tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus while calling it a countermeasure to Western escalation. This increased coercive leverage and strategic instability in Europe, moving relations further from peaceful and lawful management.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.10`, `1B.1`, `1B.5`, `1B.6`, `1B.7`

- **Title:** `ICC arrest warrants over deportation of Ukrainian children`  
  **Publisher:** International Criminal Court  
  **Date:** 17 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine](https://www.icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine)  
  **Claim-level summary:** The ICC issued arrest warrants for Putin and Maria Lvova-Belova over the unlawful deportation and transfer of Ukrainian children from occupied Ukraine. That is a major indicator that Putin’s 2023 conduct made international relations less lawful, not more.  
  **Question IDs:** `2B.10`, `2B.4`, `2B.2`

### Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2023 evidence that Putin left the regional/international order more peaceful, stable, and lawful than he inherited it. The available positive evidence is mostly formal diplomacy and rhetoric; the negative evidence is concrete and cumulative.

### Bottom line

**No.** Putin preserved some diplomatic access with China and CIS partners, but 2023 overall made regional and international relations **more dangerous and less lawful**, chiefly through continued war escalation, arms-control rupture, and coercive nuclear signaling.
